institution: Hochschule für Musik und Tanz Köln (HfMT Köln)
accreditationStatus: State university (staatliche Hochschule), degree state-recognised. Programme accreditation status UNVERIFIED
language: German (min. A2 German required for non-German-speaking degree holders; teaching in German)
whatYouStudy: Electronic and digital music; instrumental, performative or music-theatrical compositions incorporating new and latest technologies; mixed forms of instrumental and electronic composition; installations and internet works. Home of the historic Studio für Elektronische Musik.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: 'Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent'; 'Students who have not obtained their degree at a German-speaking institution must prove that they have sufficient German language skills (min. level A2)'; 'Successfully passed aptitude test'.
acceptsNonMusic: Very restrictive. VERBATIM: 'Only in exceptional cases of exceptional talent and previous education can Bachelor graduates from other art or computer science fields be admitted.' A BSc Software Engineering falls under 'computer science' but only as an exception — and the baseline is a FOUR-YEAR bachelor in composition.
portfolioSpec: Submitted works presented and discussed in a colloquium. Exact number/length/format UNVERIFIED on the English page.
auditionSpec: VERBATIM: 'The qualifying examination consists of a colloquium with the presentation and discussion of submitted works, with questions about the candidate's own musical aesthetics and prior knowledge in the field of contemporary music.'
tuitionNonEU: €0 tuition (North Rhine-Westphalia charges no tuition to non-EU students)
otherFees: Semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) — amount UNVERIFIED, typically approx. €250–300/semester in NRW incl. Semesterticket
totalCostEstimate: Tuition €0; living costs Cologne approx. €1,000–1,200/month; blocked account requirement approx. €11,904/year (2026 rate UNVERIFIED)
scholarshipName: DAAD Study Scholarships for Graduates in the Field of Music (Performing Arts)
scholarships: DAAD 'Study Scholarships – Music' (approx. €992/month plus travel and insurance; application typically Sept–Nov of the PRIOR year); Deutschlandstipendium (€300/month) — availability at HfMT Köln UNVERIFIED. No institution-specific non-EU scheme confirmed.
languageRequirement: German min. A2 (per programme page). Note: this is unusually low for a German-taught Musikhochschule Master and should be reconfirmed with the Studierendensekretariat.
deadline: UNVERIFIED — HfMT Köln aptitude exams for winter semester are typically held in spring, with applications closing around 1 March of the SAME calendar year as entry (i.e. approx. March 2027 for Sept 2027). MUST BE RECONFIRMED.

institution: Universität der Künste Berlin (UdK Berlin) — Berlin Career College
qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.) — WEITERBILDENDER (continuing-education) Master. IT IS A FULL SECOND-CYCLE M.A. DEGREE, but it is fee-funded and part-time/low-residency, run through the Berlin Career College rather than a standard consecutive Master.
accreditationStatus: Awarded by UdK Berlin, a state art university; M.A. degree status. Programme-level accreditation UNVERIFIED
durationEcts: 3 years / 6 semesters standard, low-residency part-time; an exceptional 2-year full-time condensed option exists. ECTS UNVERIFIED
whatYouStudy: Interdisciplinary between music, visual arts and media art; audio-related theory and practice; sound art as installation and performance; sound design and audiovisual media production; sound-related cultural studies, musicology, aesthetics and architecture. Alternating Basic Phase / Focus Phase / Project Phase, ending with a Master project.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: 'a low-residency, part-time postgraduate program that is aimed at professionals with a university degree or exceeding creative talent who work in the field of sound.' English proficiency required.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly open beyond music. The programme addresses professionals 'who work in the field of sound' across cultural studies, musicology, aesthetics, sound art, performance, architecture, design and media production. A BSc Software Engineering is an acceptable 'university degree' — but 'who work in the field of sound' implies some demonstrable sound practice.
portfolioSpec: No conventional music portfolio. Applicants complete 'a short admissions assignment' testing the ability to 'evaluate sound art discursively and conceptually', followed by a personal interview. Exact assignment brief UNVERIFIED.
auditionSpec: No live musical audition. VERBATIM: 'a short admissions assignment' + 'a personal interview'.
tuitionNonEU: €18,800 for the whole 3-year programme (payable in instalments) — same rate for EU and non-EU. Approx. €6,267/year.
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €18,800 tuition + approx. €1,880 semester fees over 3 years = approx. €20,700, plus Berlin living costs approx. €1,100–1,400/month
scholarshipName: UNVERIFIED — no scholarship scheme listed in the programme FAQ
scholarships: None named on the official FAQ. DAAD study scholarships generally exclude weiterbildende/fee-based programmes — MUST BE CHECKED. Deutschlandstipendium applicability UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: Proof of English proficiency required; exact test/score UNVERIFIED
englishTest: Required — specific test and minimum score UNVERIFIED
deadline: 1 February – 1 March for the following winter term (the cycle observed was 'February 1 – March 1, 2026' for winter term 2026/27). For Sept 2027 entry expect approx. 1 Feb – 1 March 2027. VPD (uni-assist preliminary review) must be submitted 8 weeks earlier.

institution: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) — Institut für Elektronische Musik und Akustik (IEM)
program: Computermusik und Klangkunst (Computer Music and Sound Art)
accreditationStatus: Public art university, curriculum published by the university; full second-cycle degree
language: German is the curricular language; the admission examination is held 'in deutscher oder englischer Sprache' (German or English). Some teaching in English at IEM. Exact language of instruction PARTLY UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: Composition and performance of electronic music, development of new electronic instruments, music informatics; deepening of theoretical knowledge and artistic skills; methods of artistic-scientific research. IEM is one of Europe's leading computer-music research institutes (Ambisonics, spatial audio).
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree required. VERBATIM (paraphrased from KUG): admission 'can only occur after the equivalence of preliminary studies is established by the dean of studies and all admission requirements are met (such as artistic audition)'.
acceptsNonMusic: NOT EXPLICITLY STATED. The equivalence of prior studies is determined case-by-case by the Studiendekan, and the decisive filter is the artistic entrance exam, not the bachelor subject. A computer-science bachelor is plausibly bridgeable here (IEM is a technical institute) but this MUST be confirmed with the Studiendekanat.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM (KUG/IEM): 'zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit' — TWO meaningful examples of artistic work (compositions, improvisations, work sketches in the field of Computermusik und Klangkunst), each approximately 5 MINUTES in duration, uploaded as audio/video files or links to a dedicated upload address (e.g. go.iem.at/iemcmkk<year>).
auditionSpec: YES — an admission colloquium. Applicants present independent compositions with electroacoustic means and/or works and must demonstrate artistic potential for the Master programme. Conducted online via Zoom as a 'Gespräch' examining motivation and research interests. (2026/27 cycle: interview 12 June 2026.)
tuitionNonEU: €726.72 per semester for third-country nationals (double the standard Austrian Studienbeitrag) = €1,453.44/year
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €1,500/year fees; Graz living costs approx. €900–1,100/month; Austrian student-visa proof-of-funds approx. €13,000–14,000/year (2027 rate UNVERIFIED)
scholarshipName: OeAD Ernst Mach Grant / Stipendien der Stipendienstiftung der Republik Österreich
scholarships: OeAD 'Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide' (approx. €1,150/month, typically for max 4 months for Master students — LIMITED USE); OeAD Scholarships of the Austrian Republic for graduate students; KUG offers Leistungsstipendien to enrolled students (amount UNVERIFIED). Tunisia is on the OeAD partner-country list — MUST BE VERIFIED for the 2027 call. Amounts/deadlines UNVERIFIED for 2027.
languageRequirement: German knowledge normally required for ordentliche Studien at Austrian universities (typically B2/C1, sometimes conditional). Exact requirement for this programme UNVERIFIED — the exam itself may be taken in English.
deadline: Application 1 March – 1 May of the entry year (i.e. approx. 1 March – 1 May 2027 for autumn 2027 entry), registration through KUGonline; entrance interview in June.

institution: Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg (HfMT Hamburg)
accreditationStatus: State university (staatliche Hochschule); full second-cycle degree. Programme accreditation UNVERIFIED
language: English — 'The lectures and other teaching formats are taught almost exclusively in English'; entrance exam conducted in English
whatYouStudy: Interactive performances, multimedia spaces, algorithmic composition, digital signal processing and live electronics; live interaction with music and video; audio-visual installations; sensors and interfaces. Modules include Artificial Models for Multimodal Creativity, Coding for Creators, Computer-aided Composition, Visual Composition in Networked Music Performance.
entryRequirements: A first degree plus the entrance examination. The programme page does not explicitly restrict the bachelor subject. Exact verbatim requirement UNVERIFIED — see Prüfungsordnung.
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES in practice — the page lists no music-degree restriction and the curriculum is heavily coding/technology oriented ('Coding for Creators'), but this is NOT stated verbatim. MUST BE CONFIRMED.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM: applicants must submit 'at least three representative works which demonstrate the ability to artistically incorporate the use of digital media, especially in the field of computer music.' Works may be 'scores, texts, recordings, computer programs, videos, etc. and/or interactive websites.' No length limit stated.
auditionSpec: YES — but no instrumental audition. A 3-hour WRITTEN exam covering (a) interactive computer music tasks, (b) text analysis/commentary, (c) multiple-choice questions on computer music terminology; plus a 15-minute interview discussing the applicant's work and motivation.
tuitionNonEU: €0 tuition (Hamburg charges no tuition to non-EU students)
otherFees: Semester contribution — amount UNVERIFIED (Hamburg typically approx. €330–350/semester incl. Semesterticket)
scholarshipName: DAAD Study Scholarships for Graduates in the Field of Music
scholarships: DAAD Music/Performing Arts study scholarship (approx. €992/month; deadline typically in the PRIOR autumn); Deutschlandstipendium (€300/month) — HfMT participation UNVERIFIED
languageRequirement: English-taught; German not required for teaching. Exact German requirement for enrolment UNVERIFIED.
englishTest: UNVERIFIED — specific test/score not stated on the programme page
deadline: UNVERIFIED. Programme starts in BOTH winter and summer semesters, which gives extra flexibility. Deadlines must be checked on hfmt-hamburg.de.

institution: Hochschule für Musik Karlsruhe — Institut für Musikinformatik und Musikwissenschaft (IMWI)
program: Musikinformatik (Music Informatics), artistic or scientific focus
qualification: Master (Master of Arts / Master of Music — exact award UNVERIFIED; SPO refers to 'Master Musikinformatik')
accreditationStatus: State university of music; full second-cycle degree per Studien- und Prüfungsordnung (SPO_MA_Musikinformatik)
language: German (an English programme page exists; actual language of instruction is German — UNVERIFIED whether English is possible)
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (ECTS UNVERIFIED from the official page)
whatYouStudy: Artistic focus: development and artistic treatment of interactive sensor-based systems; creative programming. Scientific focus: digital audio signal processing, audio software development, audio and symbol-based musical information processing. Also empirical music research, immersive 3D environments, composition, sound design for film and games. Close ties to ZKM Karlsruhe.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: admission requires 'a completed course of study in a bachelor of arts course with a major in music informatics, a combined subject in music informatics/ musicology or another relevant initial university degree, for example in music technology, electronic composition, or computer science.' Plus passing the entrance examination. 'In justified cases, outstanding professional achievements can also be recognized as qualifications in whole or in part.'
acceptsNonMusic: YES — EXPLICITLY. The entry requirement names 'computer science' as an acceptable relevant initial university degree. THIS IS ONE OF THE VERY FEW PROGRAMMES IN THE TERRITORY THAT NAMES A CS BACHELOR IN ITS OWN TEXT.
portfolioSpec: 'assessment of previously submitted work samples' (Arbeitsproben). Exact number, length and format UNVERIFIED — must be read from the SPO / Zulassungsordnung.
auditionSpec: YES — 'aptitude interview and assessment of previously submitted work samples'. No instrumental audition indicated.
tuitionNonEU: €1,500 per semester = €3,000 per year (Baden-Württemberg Landeshochschulgebührengesetz, applies to non-EU/EEA students with a foreign university entrance qualification, all BW higher education institutions)
otherFees: Semester contribution / Verwaltungsbeitrag — amount UNVERIFIED (BW typically approx. €160–200/semester)
totalCostEstimate: Approx. €3,000/year tuition + approx. €350/year fees = approx. €6,700 over 2 years, plus Karlsruhe living costs approx. €950–1,150/month
scholarships: Baden-Württemberg-Stipendium (for international students, typically €300–500/month, administered via the institution); DAAD Study Scholarships – Music; Deutschlandstipendium (€300/month). Institution-specific waivers of the €1,500 fee exist at some BW institutions for a small quota of high-performing internationals — availability at HfM Karlsruhe UNVERIFIED. Amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: German required (level UNVERIFIED, typically DSH-2 / TestDaF 4 at BW music universities)
deadline: UNVERIFIED — course starts in the winter semester; BW music universities typically close applications around 1 March–15 April of the entry year.

program: Popular Music M.A. (tracks: Performing Artist / Producing & Composing Artist / Educating Artist)
accreditationStatus: State institution of higher education (staatliche Einrichtung, Popakademie Baden-Württemberg GmbH, an accredited Hochschule); full second-cycle degree
language: German (programme delivered in German — UNVERIFIED whether English is possible)
durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, winter semester start
whatYouStudy: Popular music practice at Master level — the 'Producing & Composing Artist' track is the record-making/production route: songwriting, production, arrangement, artist development, music business. Approx. 20 places per year across the programme.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM (list of acceptable bachelor fields): 'Popmusikdesign oder Musikbusiness an der Popakademie Baden-Württemberg'; music programmes (contemporary, classical, jazz, popular music); music education; musicology, literature, cultural studies, media-related fields; art and design programmes. Plus: proof of university entrance qualification and a university degree with a minimum standard study period of 6 semesters. Plus passing the entrance examination.
acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — the listed acceptable fields extend to 'literature, cultural studies, media-related fields' and 'art and design programmes'. A BSc SOFTWARE ENGINEERING IS NOT ON THE LIST. This is a likely rejection on formal grounds unless the Popakademie grants an equivalence exception. MUST BE CONFIRMED with bewerbungmaster@popakademie.de.
portfolioSpec: Audio recordings: 3 SONGS for the Performing Artist or Educating Artist tracks; 5 SONGS for the Producing/Composing Artist track. Own compositions welcome; no stylistic guidelines. Exact file format/length not stated.
auditionSpec: YES — a full four-part entrance examination: (1) WRITTEN exam — music analysis (melody, harmony, rhythm, form, arrangement, production techniques) plus an essay on popular music history and aesthetics; (2) LIVE PERFORMANCE of 3–5 songs, maximum 15 minutes total, own or cover; (3) musical ad-hoc accompaniment demonstrating flexibility across popular styles; (4) oral interview on musical qualifications and motivation.
tuitionNonEU: €1,500 per semester = €3,000/year (Baden-Württemberg non-EU tuition) — UNVERIFIED whether the Popakademie applies the LHGebG rate or its own; MUST BE CONFIRMED
totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED pending confirmation of the non-EU rate
scholarships: Baden-Württemberg-Stipendium; Deutschlandstipendium — participation UNVERIFIED. No Popakademie-specific non-EU scheme confirmed.
deadline: 30 APRIL each year (documents must be submitted online by 30 April to take part in the entrance examination) — i.e. 30 April 2027 for a September 2027 start. NOTE: this is the SAME-YEAR deadline, not the prior cycle.

institution: Folkwang Universität der Künste — Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien (ICEM)
qualification: Master (Master of Music / Master of Arts — exact award UNVERIFIED; see Prüfungsordnung Master Integrative Komposition)
accreditationStatus: State art university; full second-cycle degree. Programme accreditation UNVERIFIED
whatYouStudy: Four focus areas: instrumental composition, ELECTRONIC composition, composition and visualisation, and pop composition. ICEM (founded 1990) is the oldest interdisciplinary institute of Folkwang and one of Germany's established computer-music centres.
entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED in detail — set out in the Prüfungsordnung Master Integrative Komposition. Known: VERBATIM 'Master Studierende müssen sich mit einem Vorschlag für ein (großes!) Projekt bewerben, das sie während ihres Studiums umsetzen wollen' — Master applicants must apply WITH A PROPOSAL FOR A LARGE PROJECT they intend to realise during their studies, ideally combining several of the specialisations.
acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — not stated on the ICEM page.
portfolioSpec: A proposal for a large project to be realised during the studies, plus (presumably) prior works. Exact number/length/format UNVERIFIED — read the Prüfungsordnung.
otherFees: Semester contribution UNVERIFIED (NRW typically approx. €300/semester incl. Semesterticket)
scholarships: DAAD Study Scholarships – Music; Deutschlandstipendium — Folkwang participation UNVERIFIED
